terms.binding_label: Requirements treated as binding for clinical-variant volume
terms.restricted_note: keeping regulated parts with qualified suppliers

text.company_blurb: A fictional medical-device maker (bedside monitor, infusion pump, handheld ultrasound)
text.rules_note: Supplier controls come from 21 CFR Part 820 (FDA QMSR, effective 2 Feb 2026, incorporating ISO 13485 purchasing controls). Wireless parts matter because connected devices fall under FD&C Act s524B cybersecurity rules (SBOM, vulnerability plan). Customer contracts add attestations. All are screening inputs, not legal conclusions. Company, parts and prices are synthetic. Rules last reviewed 2026-11-14 (see Regulatory outlook for sources).
text.spares_note: Field-service parts often cost more for good reasons (small lots, fast delivery). No typical medical spares markup is published, so treat this as a prompt to ask, not a verdict.
text.rules_change_example: Rules change (e.g. a pending Section 232 decision on medical devices could add tariffs on imported parts).
text.pilot_scope: one consenting device maker, one product family, 2 to 3 BOM revisions, purchased assemblies and recurring spares
match_notes: **Text alone** auto-accepts about 77% of part lines with zero wrong; **supplier-SKU history** (a SKU confirmed once vouches for its other lines) lifts that to {auto_share}.
The second-industry pack reuses the identical matching engine; only vocabulary and rule labels differ.
